wire.operator_setup.prompt.confirm_phone.role: Operating-system administrator prompt reason (macOS shows it inside the system password dialog)
wire.operator_setup.prompt.confirm_phone.note: Shown by the OS itself next to the password field, so the person sees WHY their computer password is asked for. One sentence. 'Local Operator' is the product name: keep it. Must not mention Radient: this is the computer's own password.

wire.operator_setup.refused.privileged.note: Classify by stable code/status, not text. Nothing was changed when this shows. Never mention 'anchor', 'sudo' or 'pkexec'.

wire.operator_setup.refused.terminal_can.role: Terminal-app refusal: this terminal app cannot hand the screen to the computer's password prompt
wire.operator_setup.refused.terminal_can.note: Classify by stable code/status, not text. Nothing was changed when this shows. Never mention 'anchor', 'sudo' or 'pkexec'. The cause is THIS TERMINAL APP, not the computer: the desktop app on the same computer may still work, which is why it is named. Keep 'Settings → Phone access' as the desktop app's menu path.

wire.operator_setup.outcome.file_only.role: Security caveat shown as its own notice after phone approvals turn on, on a computer whose approval key is a plain file
wire.operator_setup.outcome.file_only.note: Shown right under 'Phone approvals are on. Each new phone will still ask for your computer's password once.' The lead-in ('Note: on this computer itself') makes clear this caveat is about approving ON THIS COMPUTER, not about phones, so the two sentences do not read as contradicting each other. Keep the lead-in's meaning.

wire.operator_setup.tui.usage.role: Terminal app usage line for the /mobile approvals command
wire.operator_setup.tui.usage.note: '/mobile approvals on' is a typed command: keep it exactly, untranslated, and keep it at the END of the sentence with no period after it, so it is never read or copied together with the surrounding words.

wire.operator_setup.tui.starting.role: Terminal app progress line shown just before the computer's password prompt

wire.operator_setup.tui.approvals_report.role: Terminal-app report line for /approvals when the session asks before tools run, config.yml says auto, and phone approvals are not set up on this computer
wire.operator_setup.tui.approvals_report.note: ONE full sentence, translated whole, so it never switches language halfway. Starts lowercase like the sibling report lines ('tool approvals: …'). {live} and {saved} are approval-mode words ('ask'/'auto') and 'config.yml', '/approvals {saved}' and '/mobile approvals on' are typed text: keep them exactly. 'neither' refers to the two ways to approve: on this machine (Touch ID) or from a paired phone. Keep 'Settings → Phone access' as the app's menu path.
